title: GrantScout: matched UK grant digest for small businesses

problem_severity_frequency.rationale: Finding and winning grant funding is time-consuming and competitive (GOV.UK), and SMEs frequently ask about it; the pain looked strong before the adversarial pass.

buyer_budget_clarity.rationale: SME owners and their accountants have budget and incentive, but category pricing is anchored to free government search and contingency-fee advisers.

evidence_strength.rationale: A primary government source plus live vendor pages; competitor success-rate claims are self-reported and unverified.

distribution.rationale: Accountant channel, business networks and SEO/benchmark content are plausible non-paid routes, but unmeasured.

differentiation.rationale: GovOwed already sells the exact flat-fee match/report wedge; GOV.UK's free service undercuts discovery. Little differentiation survives.

validation_speed_cost.rationale: A cheap landing-page/digest test with a pre-fixed decision rule could have produced a decisive read within a week.

feasibility.rationale: Assembling and maintaining a UK grant digest is straightforward; the blocker is positioning, not build.

economics.rationale: Competing against £0 government search and £29 one-time incumbent pricing leaves little room for a recurring subscription.

founder_fit.rationale: No evidence recorded about founder domain access to SMEs, accountants or grant funding; left unscored rather than guessed.

risk.rationale: Low regulatory risk using public grant data; main risk is commoditisation by free government tools and cheap incumbents.

economic_buyer.note: SME owner or their accountant has budget and a clear incentive to win grant funding.

painful_frequent_or_budgeted.note: Grant discovery and application is time-consuming with long, competitive processes (GOV.UK).

non_paid_distribution.note: Accountant channel, business networks and SEO/benchmark content are credible non-paid routes (assumption, not yet measured).

defensible_wedge.note: At desk-screen a curated UK-grant digest with plain-language eligibility looked like a usable wedge; later contested and vetoed.

no_network_effects_needed.note: A grant database is usable by a single customer; no network requirement.

plausible_margins.note: A £15-£29/mo subscription was modelled to cover low content costs (assumption, untested against real CAC).

acceptable_risk.note: Uses public funding data; no regulated personal data beyond contact details.

cheap_disconfirming_test.note: A cheap landing-page/digest test with a pre-fixed decision rule can falsify the wedge.

not_all_optimistic.note: Stop rules are defined; no single optimistic assumption carries the whole case.

vetoes.note: Adversarial pass: the exact flat-fee grant-matching wedge is already occupied by GovOwed at £29 one-time / £499 per year, while the authoritative alternative (GOV.UK Find a grant) is free and category pricing is anchored to contingency/no-win-no-fee. No defensible wedge survives.
